text:
I am thankful for a lot of things in life, but my family is the best thing that has ever happened to me.

The two most common things people said to me before having kids is that it's better than anyone can explain to you and it goes very fast; these are both true and I don't have much to add. But I am very grateful and I love them more than there is any way to explain.

Also I cannot really imagine life without Ollie and I think without his unwavering support and great advice I would have gone crazy by now.

🦃

Oh, one thing about kids:

Most good things get a little less satisfying the 100th time you do them.

A quiet evening hanging out with your kids, even doing very mundane stuff, is in the rare category of something repetitive just getting better and better.

Ven was one of the earliest believers that we could use our then-current model to solve millenium prize problems.

There are a lot of brilliant people in the world, but being brilliant and also having correctly-placed confidence and courage to keep pushing on something that others don't think is possible is a very valuable thing and fairly rare.

I am grateful so many people at OpenAI have this combination.

text:
Brian Chesky used to ask Airbnb candidates if they'd take the job with a year left to live:

"I interviewed the first 300 employees at Airbnb, which people think I'm really neurotic, and that may also be true... I used to ask them, 'If you had a year left to live, would you take this job?' And actually the people who say yes to that you probably don't want because they should probably spend time with [their] family. So I amended it to 10 years."

"I really wanted people to think about that. That was enough time for you to do something you really cared about. And the answer doesn't have to be this company. And I say, 'Fine, if what you're meant to do is to travel... you should just do that. Don't come here. Go do that.'"

"Two men are laying bricks. Somebody comes up to the first man and says, 'What are you doing?' He says, 'I'm building a wall.' He asks the other guy, 'What are you doing?' He says, 'I'm building a cathedral.'"

"There is a job, and then there's a calling. And we want to hire people that aren't just looking for jobs. They're looking for a calling. And that's kind of the first value, and that's champion the mission."

@bchesky at Stanford, 2014

Amjad Masad on the delusional self-belief that kept him from selling Replit:

"We started getting acquisition offers literally the same year we started... It ramped up pretty quickly."

"But I was insane enough to say no, although it would've been not only life-changing money for me... It would change my entire lineage, my entire family, my entire country."

"It's just this delusional self-belief. And so far it's been working out."

@amasad on Second Time Founders Podcast, 2023

Patrick Collison's advice to people in their 20s: find where the highest standards are, and go experience them firsthand.

"When I talk to people in other domains, this is so frequently the thing that I hear from them."

"That when they worked with X person or Y organization or in Z environment, they learned what great actually is, and that just permanently changed their sense for what their own standard for their work ought to be."

"Maybe one version of what people in their twenties should do is... figure out, where can you learn the highest standards? Where are the highest standards embodied, and where can you go and experience that firsthand?"

@patrickc with @dwarkesh_sp, 2024

Ben Horowitz on why asking whether AI is good or bad misses the point:

"I always like to go back to a quote from Andy Grove, which I absolutely love, which he said in the '90s. And somebody asked him, 'Andy, is the microprocessor good or bad?' And he said, 'Well, that's not even the right question. That's like asking, is steel good or bad? It is. And so it's our job to make it good.'"

"You can't get rid of the wheel now. It's over. It's here. You can't get rid of AI now. It's over. It's here. You can't outlaw math."

"So then the real question is, what do we have to do to make it good and positive for society? And by the way, without new technologies, how are we going to deal with pandemics or climate change or any of the real issues facing the world?"

@bhorowitz with @eriktorenberg on Turpentine VC, 2023

A robot’s next move depends on what it knows about the object in front of it. 🦾

PhysCaP helps robots estimate an object’s weight and softness by lifting and squeezing it. Those measurements guide what to check next and when the robot has enough information to act.

Developed with NVIDIA Research, the approach reduced the number of physical checks and the time needed to complete tabletop tasks.

Read the paper and get the code 🔗 https://nvda.ws/3WQPCkr
